title: SRE incident communications skeleton (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, role-oriented draft runbook for incident communications. It includes: status page templates, quick customer notices, escalation rules for tenant-impacting events, and an internal war-room checklist. Use this as the source for fast, consistent comms during incidents.

Audience:
- Primary: SRE on-call, Incident Commander (IC), Communications lead
- Secondary: Product owners, Support, Solutions Engineering, Account teams (for high-severity customer impact)

When to use this doc (quick decision):
- Use for any incident where customer-visible degradation occurs or where broader engineering involvement is required.
- If impact is internal-only (no user-visible degradation) follow internal-only comms (short Slack note + incident ticket).

Role quick reference:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns updates cadence, triage decisions, authorizes public messages.
- Communications lead: drafts public-facing text, coordinates customer-facing stakeholders.
- Tech lead: runs mitigation, provides short rationale for updates.
- Support/CS liaison: prepares account-specific notices for affected customers.

Channels and templates (use verbatim and customize placeholders):
1) Status page short update (public):
- Template: [short timeline style]
  - Title: "{service} – {short-impact} (Incident {INCIDENT_ID})"
  - Status: Investigating | Identified | Mitigating | Service Degraded | Resolved
  - Impact: "Some users may experience {symptom} for {subset} (e.g., region, API endpoint)."
  - Next update: "We will provide an update by {ETA} or sooner."
  - Details: one short sentence: "Initial signals from internal metrics/alerts indicate {root_signal}."
  - Link: "For more details see: {incident-brd-link}"

- Example: "Redwood API – increased 5xx errors for /v1/generate in us-west (Incident RWI-2026-042). Status: Investigating. Impact: Some requests to text generation may return 5xx; retries may succeed. Next update: 20 minutes. For details: {incident-link}."

2) Status page detailed update (public, 2nd+ update):
- Template:
  - Status: Identified / Mitigating
  - Impact: More detail on affected routes/customers/regions
  - Root cause hypothesis: short technical line (no internal logs or sensitive info)
  - Mitigation in progress: numbered bullets of actions being taken
  - ETA: expected window to next milestone or rollback plan
  - Customer action: recommended short steps (e.g., backoff + retry, use alternate region)
  - Contacts: link to support/ops channel and incident link

3) Customer-facing incident email/DM (for impacted customers):
- When: Severity P1/P2 with clear tenant impact or SLA implications.
- Sender: Support/CS + IC copy.
- Subject: "Redwood – Service interruption affecting {feature} (Incident {INCIDENT_ID})"
- Body template (short):
  "Hello {CustomerName},

  We are actively investigating an issue affecting {product/endpoint} that may impact your {examples: embeddings, text generation}. Our engineers have identified {brief cause/hypothesis} and are working to restore full service. At this time you may see {symptoms}.

  What we are doing: {live mitigation bullets}.
  ETA / next update: {ETA}.

  Your assigned support rep: {support_name} ({support_email}). We will provide a post-incident report when resolved.

  Apologies for the disruption,
  Redwood Inference Operations
"

- Notes: Keep technical details minimal. Do not include internal stack traces or raw logs. If there is a contractual impact, include CS/Legal in cc.

4) Internal Slack/Bridge short blast (for company):
- Template: "[INCIDENT {INCIDENT_ID}] {service} – {Status} – Quick summary (1 line). IC: {name}. Bridge: {bridge-link}. Public status: {status-link}. Next update: {ETA}."

- Use pinned message in the incident channel with runbook link, timeline doc, and on-call roster.

Escalation guidance (triage flow):
- If >5% of requests or core feature is impacted, treat as P1.
- Key escalation steps:
  - IC oncall -> page IC if not already present.
  - If customer SLA at risk or major enterprise tenant affected, page CS lead and Sales engineering.
  - If incident spans multiple regions or services, request cross-functional war-room: infra, runtime, product, CS.

Internal war-room checklist (fast pace, use as checklist):
1) Spin up bridge and create incident ticket: record INCIDENT_ID (e.g., RWI-2026-042). Link to ticket in channel.
2) Assign roles: IC, scribe, comms lead, tech lead, CS liaison, postmortem owner.
3) Initial public status: publish Investigating short update to status page + internal channel.
4) Capture data points: last good deploy, traffic graphs, error rates, request traces, recent config changes, capacity events. Note owners for each artifact.
5) Contain first: apply safe mitigation (traffic reroute, soft-fail, rollback, scale-up). Mark actions with timestamps and actor.
6) Confirm recovery criteria (what metrics indicate healthy).
7) If mitigation succeeds, move to 'Mitigating' then 'Resolved' in status page sequence.
8) Document timeline live in incident ticket (earliest symptom -> detection -> mitigation -> resolution).
9) Post-incident: schedule postmortem within 7 business days, assign author, collect action items.

Checklist tips: prefer short bullets, use checkboxes in incident ticket, use timestamps in ISO format, avoid speculative language in public updates.

Templates for short status cadence (example cadence):
- 0 min: Investigating (short public + internal blast).
- 15–30 min: Identified/Mitigating (what we're doing + ETA).
- 60 min: Update with progress or escalate communications frequency (every 30m).
- Close: Resolved + short summary + postmortem promise + link to follow-up.

Decision tree: who to notify externally
- If only internal jobs failing and no customer-visible errors -> internal only.
- If customer-visible errors for <5% of requests and retry mitigates -> update status page with investigating + guidance; no mass email.
- If a named customer is impacted or SLA at risk -> notify CS + send customer email.
- If multiple customers or core APIs are impacted -> send mass customer email and coordinate with account teams.

Language and tone guidance (short):
- Public: concise, factual, non-speculative, apologies when appropriate, visible ownership and ETA.
- Customer emails: empathetic, concrete next steps, CS contact info, commitment to a postmortem.
- Internal: more technical details allowed, but mark sensitive info as internal-only.

Common pitfalls (avoid):
- Using jargon in customer messages (no internal error codes).
- Over-promising ETAs.
- Leaving long gaps without updates if customers are impacted.

Post-incident comms checklist:
- Publish final status page update with root cause summary and timeline.
- Send targeted customer follow-ups to impacted tenants with remediation/credits info if applicable.
- Produce a blameless postmortem and share with stakeholders.
- Implement prioritized action items and track in Jira with owners and ETA.

Appendix: quick copy-paste snippets
- Investigating (status page):
  "Status: Investigating. We are aware of increased errors affecting {service}. Engineers are actively investigating. Next update: {ETA}."

- Identified (status page):
  "Status: Identified. Root cause: {short-hypothesis}. Mitigation: {what we are doing}. Impact: {scope}. ETA: {ETA}."

- Resolved (status page):
  "Status: Resolved. We have restored full service for {service}. Root cause: {summary}. We will publish a post-incident report with details and action items."

Notes to authors (drafting):
- Keep this doc order-of-importance: speed over completeness. Replace placeholders before publishing. Use incident ticket as single source of truth for timeline and artifacts.

Open questions / TODOs in this draft:
- Define severity thresholds by absolute numbers (requests/min) and by tenant percent impact.
- Template for enterprise account SRE-to-Customer technical deep dive (post-resolution).
- Automate status page publish from incident ticket (investigate tooling).

Last edits log:
- 2025-11-05: initial skeleton (Jordan K.).
- 2026-01-12: added cadence suggestions and customer email template (Aisha P.).
- 2026-02-10: clarified escalation rules and added linked artifacts examples (Marco R.).

End of document.
